review:
This game is weird. It's like one of those sports-themed animes with all the character growth that comes from victories and defeats alike, and it has a Phoenix Wright aspect in how the story is driven by a lot of dialogue between hand-drawn characters with little animation. Boiled down to its bare bones it's 3-on-3 rugby and a lot of reading, but somehow it's still fun? Yeah, I told you it's weird. 

You can't really make any right or wrong choices, but it's still excruciating having to decide who goes free and who stays with your party for future rites. If the game was shorter, I would have gone for a third playthrough to see what happens with more defeats and another set of decisions. Maybe I still will. But I'm also hooked to my party shouting "NOXALAS", so making it unnecessariily harder feels like betraying all these likeable characters.

Pyre is nothing like SGG's other games. Or any other game I've played. Give it a shot (or a plunge) if a non-deterministic visual novel that only requires you to play along without the need to win could appeal to you.

This is, at its core, a simple sports game with a fantasy aesthetic. I'm not a sports fan in basically any respect, but the story, characters, and worldbuilding kept me hooked through two playthroughs. The fact that there's no real fail condition makes the story unique without diminishing any of the stakes. If you like other Supergiant games, there's no reason not to give this one a shot.

Steam Deck: Perfect
Gameplay: Lots of reading between short games of rugby.
Replayability: No

There is no right/wrong/good/bad decisions or results, it all pushes the story along in the same direction with slight narrative differences.

The rugby is either too easy or obscenely hard (with most/all mods on).

This is my favorite Supergiant game. In Pyre, you gather a group of outcasts to form a fantasy basketball team playing for a chance to ascend from a sort of hell-on-earth to the exalted city of your overlords. You field three of your party members in each match. Each party member moves across the playing field differently and had different special abilities. Your opponents are fully realized characters who you can feel conflicted about  beating, thereby condemning them to stay in hell.  The voice acting, music, and writing are all of the quality you'd expect from the studio behind Hades. It's a wonder to me that more people haven't played this. Pyre is ripe for a sequel or a refresh and I hope Supergiant tackles it some day.

Supergiant fans and the broader critical sphere are living in some alternate dimension, I swear to God. All this time I had heard that Pyre was the worst Supergiant game, when actually it's the best one. Pyre oozes with SOUL. The gameplay and story are both excellent. This actually has heart and ambition and artistic worth to it. More games in Pyre's vein should have been made, instead of selling out to mainstream tastes and making not only a roguelite, but a SEQUEL to said roguelike.

Сюжет - это самая круто наполненная игра от этой студии в плане сценария и сюжета. Большое количество персонажей и они намного более раскрыты чем в других играх. Такое обилие персонажей и сеттинг заставляет выбирать как ими пользоваться, с кем говорить, чьи предложения слушать, в каком порядке и кого отправлять наверх , в конце будет рассказано о каждом на манер конечной заставки фолычей. И вот это реально аргумент для реиграбельности, потому что вариантов крайне немало, и это хочется узнать, ибо персонажи притягательны, проработаны, и РАСКРЫТЫ , чего не хватало бастиону и транзистору. я считаю со сценарной точки зрения это лучшая игра от этой студии.

Ok, what do I say about Pyre? I don't recall when I last played something this unique. If you're like me, and you played all the rest of Supergiant's games first - do NOT skip this one. And if you haven't played any of their games, this is an amazing one to start with. Pyre stands out, even from their wonderful catalogue, that's for sure.

So yeah, it's a sports-based RPG. And it's really fricking good at that. Reducing the gameplay to its most simplistic core (and trust me, that's doing it a disservice), you generally have two parts:

1) The Rites, which are kind of like superpower-enhanced games of basketball, if you will. Two pyres (the "baskets"), two teams, one fallen star (your "ball"). Get the star into your opponent's Pyre. Obviously, there's a whole lot more to it than that - a ton of different characters with different stats, abilities, small skill trees, environmental factors etc. It's super easy to pick up, but also has an incredible skill ceiling, meaning everybody can have a blast, whether you're someone new to this type of gameplay or someone who has 5000 hours in Rocket League.

2) The "story" part between the Rites, during which you travel through the lands, plan your route, make decisions, meet characters and hang out with your triumvirate, the Nightwings. This part is kinda like a visual novel. There's very little voice acting, and as such, a fair bit of reading (unsurprising, given the protagonist being called "Reader"). Needless to say: the writing is great, all characters feel unique, you'll quickly find yourself caring for a lot of them and the narrative style is truly an experience. One that you have a huge part in influencing yourself. But, if you are somebody who does not like games with slower pacing and visual novel-style aspects, then you might want to reconsider. It's like an amazing movie - no matter how good it is, if someone doesn't like sitting in front of a screen for 2 hours, the experience might not be for them.

Pyre is a unique game. While previous Supergiant games were somewhat straightforward, a different flavors of RPG, Pyre is a mix of a party based RPG, a visual novel and a sports game. The mix is weird, some elements work, some work to the detriment of the overall experience.

The story of Pyre takes place in the Downside, which serves as a prison for the nation of Commonwealth. Your character, unnamed and unseen, becomes an exile due to the greatest crime of all - being able to read. For unknown reasons, Commonwealth govermant has a widespread ban on literacy and shows them instantly as a tyrannical authocracy that holds lesser people under the threat of exile. Our character is saved by a strange trio of a giant horned demon lady, anthropomorhic talking dog, and a regular guy from Middle East. Long story short, all of you have formed the triumvirate of Nightwings, and will participate in the rites to free themslves from exile and return to the Commonwealth. Unfortunately, knowing the rules of Commonwealth, it is not as easy as it seems and there are quite a few of prerequisites and unclear rules on how to actually gain your freedom through the Rites.
The story is good, but it becomes a bit dense at a certain point. Writers definitely put a lot of thought into the world and the lore. There are way more characters than previous Supergiant Games. There is a whole book that explains lore and has a full index of each of the races, scribes, triumvirates, locations and so on. Unfortunately, checking all of this out takes a lot and unless you are super into this world, you will be skimming over all of the additional lore that is provided. Not to mention the lack of voice acting. Each of the characters talks in their own way of gibberish with only the judge talking during the rites. There will be a lot of reading. 
What doesn't help is the structure of the story. First half of the game is a rather linear adventure, where you meet new party members, new rival triumvirates, and travel through new locations. But, after first leg of the journey ends, the map opens up and the structure of the games changes and becomes a bit repetitive. Knowing that, the game speeds up and basically forces you into an endgame, causing uneven pacing with a pretty slow and measured start and rushing to the finish line. 

The presentation of the game is on point. The character designs are great and serve the baseline that will be expanded upon in Hades. The world map presented as a storybook with each new location unfolding before you. The music is still amazing, with each character having their own unique theme on top of the great ambient tracks and more upbeat tracks playing during the rites. The only limitation is the amount of sprites characters have during conversations. Each character gets only one pose with different facial expressions, with only variation having their Nightwing garments and regular clothes, but there are a lot of characters, so it's understandable.

The gameplay is where it gets a bit more weird. The structure of the game is simple. You get a destination towards the next rite, travel to that location and a long the way choose the path, which may provide new resources or buffs, or provide you the time to pursue your vocations, which allow you to gather resources, get permament buffs, or level up one of the characters. Then you get to the rite itself and participate in the weirdest game of basketball. Each team gets three represantatives, each character belongs to a different race, each having different stats, movement and abilities related to their aura. First three characters represent this dichotomy perfectly, with demon Jodariel having the biggest aura and doing the most damage to the enemy pyre, while cur Rukey is the fastes, but having smaller aura with doing the least damage, with the nomad Hedwyn being balanced character in-between. 
After you choose your characters the goal is simple, get the ball in the middle of the map, and get it to the enemy pyre to douse it's flames. Your character can just jump into the pyre to do full damage, but then you will lose them in the next round, or throw the ball into the flames, but charging it to the full power takes time and can be blocked by the enemy. Each character can level up by gaining the experience after the rite which can enhance their abilities. After the initial novelty wears off, the whole process gets pretty repetitive. While there is a signature Supergiant games mechanic of adding optional challenges for a bigger reward, the reward this time is just more experience points for faster leveling, and it doesn't change the core gameplay that much.

There is also a versus mode where two players can locally participate in the rites, so if you are really into the rite gameplay, you can get into the metagame of the rites, but I don't think there is a big community for the Pyre pro-gameplay. 

So yeah, Pyre is weird and can get somewhat boring and repetitive during the later stages of the game. But It's a very unique experience worth chacking out. As a fan of Supergiant Games, I am pretty satisfied overall with this one.

На момент знайомства з Pyre я вже пройшов Bastion і Transistor, і вже був знайомий трохи зі стилем Supergiant Games. Коротко - третя гра від цього розробника змогла перевершити обидві попередні (що логічно, послідовно, але все одно приємно).

Описувати кожен окремий штрих, який вплинув на загальну оцінку, я мабуть не буду. Якщо грали у вищезгадані ігри, і вам сподобалося - Pyre вам теж сподобається (наскільки - це вже інше питання). Якщо не грали - краще почніть із якоїсь із них, для того, щоб потім отримати додаткове задоволення від того, як розвивається манера подавати історію від гри до гри. 

Графіка - традиційно спочатку дуже незвична, але швидко починає сприйматися органічно. Стиль - традиційно унікальний для кожної гри. Не знаю, хто в Supergiant продав душу сатані, але у них ще є кілька років у запасі. 

Музичний супровід - традиційно Darren Korb і Ashley Barrett, і десяток різних ненав'язливих мелодій, які сидітимуть в голові ще декілька днів після проходження гри. 

Гра традиційно не поспішає розкривати історію, і певний час ми, як завжди, будемо нічого не розуміти, всі будуть тикати на нас пальцями, але якщо з усіма говорити, і тикати на все інтерактивне, то до кінця гри вибудується і доволі значний лор, і розкриються всі ключові персонажі. І от по цим моментам Pyre суттєво перевершив попередні ігри. 

Ну і нарешті ігровий процес. Він незвичний, до нього треба звикати (і краще трохи налаштувати керування під себе), але як тільки звикнеш, дивуєшся, як у когось можуть виникати з ним проблеми. 

На високій складності гра традиційно важка, ближче до кінця я здався і перейшов на найлегшу складність, щоб закінчити історію. Що поробиш, старий уже став, реакція не та. Але завершення гри було того варте. 

Що в цілому? Гра дуже сподобалася, і від десятки її відділяє лише чималий перелік моментів, пов'язаних із основним ігровим заняттям, де гра трактувала правила по одному, а я (і мої очікування) - по іншому. Багато таких ситуацій, і вони бісять, бо гра складна й сама по собі, не треба додатково підігравати супротивникам. 
Але навіть наявність такого, доволі суттєвого моменту, не змогла опустити оцінку більше ніж на бал. 
Pyre - пройдена, і попереду лишаються лише два шедеври зі спільною назвою Hades...

I can't believe I've never reviewed this game.
Pyre is one of the most special gaming experiences I've ever had. It was drawn down a little by my disdain for "sportsball" kinds of games, but the unique twist of auras being equally lethal to all and having different shapes/formations/movements made even that gameplay fun, and even stressful. 
The real meat of the game is it's story, which is extremely personal to the player. Without any spoilers, I'll tell you this: You hold the future of your closest companions in your hand. While initially they may seem odd or uninteresting, as the game progresses and you complete a number of rites, it becomes very difficult to ignore their different personality quirks and ways of looking at the world. This is a game that thrusts a responsibility onto you that, by the end, will have you struggling to rationalize certain actions - because every win and every loss has an effect. At some points, losing a rite on purpose might be something you find yourself doing, if you're like me. 

This game's soundtrack is a blessing to the ears, just like in every Supergiant game, with Darren Korb and Ashley Barrett absolutely knocking it out of the park (and, as is now tradition, cameoing in the game as a pair of divine bards). 

If you're on the fence about Pyre, ask yourself what you want more: If it's 'intensely deep gameplay mechanics', it might not be for you. If it's 'a story that forces you into a gripping situation that has you questioning how it'll end', then it absolutely is for you.

[h1] Games where freedom and eternal exile are at stake. [/h1]

[hr][/hr]

[quote] 📝 Narrative and its text [/quote]

The entire premise of this narrative is well presented: an underworld of exiles who disobeyed the dictatorship above, who now, through games, must overcome each other for a chance to return home. There's a lot of context to give to this fantasy through text; I confess that many answers went unnoticed for me, sometimes there's so much information that it's difficult to make sense of every little thing.

Like Bastion, Supergiant returns with a text full of minutiae and unusual words, something that is sometimes difficult to follow. This is even more contrasting than the first game, as Pyre revolves heavily around dialogue and writing, which are as intrinsic to the gameplay loop as a visual novel.

Despite the complicated text, the narrative flows very well most of the time. I think the most negative aspect for me is the Book of Rites, an encyclopedia about that universe and its mysticism. The information in the book is very fragmented and somewhat random. I skimmed through everything I unlocked, but after a while I was so out of touch with some things that it almost snowballed into disinterest.

Throughout the journey, mysteries are introduced. I liked the things related to the old Nightwings team, others not so much, for example, the hints the game gives that certain possibilities are open, but then nothing of real significance ever happens, in my opinion.

[spoiler] It ends a bit underwhelming. I would have liked to see, and not just read about, certain events that are presented as the central objective throughout the journey. At least a lot of context is given about them, but it still didn't fill that gap for me. [/spoiler]

Ultimately, this narrative showed a lot of potential, but for me, it left a feeling of underdeveloped themes and events.

[quote] ☁ Freedom for the players [/quote]

We have a very intriguing cast of characters here; one of the best things about the game is seeing the relationships between them, with very different personalities on the same team. Sometimes it even seems like too many, as the game sidelines some of them for a considerable amount of time (although this has to do with some minor choices).

There's a very interesting duality in the 'liberation' options we have, as we have to choose between those we like most in terms of gameplay and story. At first, it feels bad to send them to freedom, as I feel I lose potential connection with and between them. Sometimes the "worst" (with the gameplay I liked least) players on my team were the ones rewarded with the greatest gift from that underworld.

According to the "Making of," the studio wanted to convey an analogy with players on teams leaving, and I think they managed to do that very well.

These choices are certainly one of the game's high points; the consequences are handled masterfully.

[quote] ⚽, 🏀, 🏈, 🤼 ? [/quote]

Like previous experiences, the studio once again creates something extremely unique for its action, in this case, a kind of football + American football + basketball + hints of wrestling.

Initially, this sports element is quite straightforward; with the introduction of new players to our team, things get a little more interesting, but in my view, it never scales that well.

Since they stay in the same spot, it's basically a one-man game; the others function as backups after another player is eliminated or a score is reached. I think some potentially assisted team strategies don't work so well, such as placing a player forward while the ball is back there to then make a pass, because the opponents focus on that character immediately, making it practically impossible to do so. Speaking of passes, this is an option that didn't have much function in my playthrough, just like shooting the ball, which is very slow; I never saw the need to use this mechanic.

The AI is sometimes inconsistent, doing very dynamic things (including showing us powerful new strategies), but other times doing very stupid things, like standing still when we're approaching the objective or even scoring fewer points than they could if they chose another option. Another thing is the rather large number of talismans for only 1 slot; opponents also possess some, and you can even see them to devise a possible strategy, but it's something I never paid attention to. Perhaps this talisman “issue” could be interesting against another player, but against the CPU, what they have is somewhat irrelevant.

Because of all this, this central functionality of the game felt a bit one-sided to me, as the strategy is always basically the same, especially since we never have a reason to do something different from what's working.

Despite this, I can't say I didn't have fun. With the titans active, even doing similar things, some games were exciting. Furthermore, the characters differ just the right amount; almost all of them contain new things, as well as similarities in gameplay, which in this case is good because we lose several of them and thus are not forced to use those with characteristics that we don't like.

Es básicamente baloncesto, pero con un orbe caído del cielo y en el que utilizas las habilidades de cada uno de tus compañeros. Sobre el papel parece sencillo, pero tiene mucha estrategia (como por ejemplo, hacer que Rukey haga un sprint y meta el orbe en la pira esquivando a tus enemigos :P) y es muy divertido. En fin, que me enrollo: Pyre es un juego sobresaliente que simplemente necesita de más atención. Que la obra maestra que es Hades no tape a los demás títulos del estudio.

Pyre is a sports game. You play as a reader who reads the stars for the Nightwing team. You are an exile, together with your team and your adversaries in the Downside. Only through the rites can any of you be free. The game works like a visual novel, with the sports game in between that would change the course of the outcome.

Overall, the game is really good: story, lore, music, pacing, etc. I especially like the story and the lore of it. It's a well-told story and the lore about the eight scribes and your motivation for winning the game are wonderful.

The only weakness, although this might be a big one, is the matches/rites themselves. I suspect this is because they want to make this a PvP game. Therefore, they had to make the game fair and real-time for both teams. I would prefer if there is more strategic layer to them, such as having a turn-based action, pause, or controlling multiple characters at once.

But still, it is still a great game with great story and I recommend this.

[b]Pyre[/b] blends visual novel storytelling with a unique ritual-based competitive system, creating a mechanically distinctive experience built around positioning, timing, and strategic sacrifice.

[b]CORE RITE MECHANICS[/b]

[*][b]3v3 Ritual Battles[/b] - Each Rite plays like a hybrid of sports and tactical arena combat, where positioning and orb control determine victory.
[*][b]Pyre & Orb System[/b] - Carrying the orb extinguishes the enemy flame but leaves you vulnerable, creating constant risk vs reward decisions.
[*][b]Aura Abilities[/b] - Each character has unique movement speed, jump arcs, and special abilities that define tactical roles.
[*][b]Downed State Mechanics[/b] - Banished characters temporarily leave the field, shifting team momentum dynamically.

[b]TEAM COMPOSITION & STRATEGY[/b]

[*]Character synergies matter — speed, size, and abilities combine into different tactical approaches.
[*]Selecting your trio before each Rite becomes a strategic decision based on opponent tendencies.
[*]Movement control and spacing are more important than raw aggression.

[b]PROGRESSION & SACRIFICE SYSTEM[/b]

[*]Winning Rites can permanently free a character, removing them from your roster.
[*]This creates meaningful long-term mechanical consequences tied directly to success.
[*]Progression isn’t just stat-based — it reshapes available strategies over time.

[b]RISK, MOMENTUM & PLAYER AGENCY[/b]

[*]Matches swing based on timing, orb steals, and defensive positioning.
[*]You can choose to win or intentionally lose certain Rites, affecting narrative and roster mechanics.
[*]Every decision carries mechanical and long-term impact.

[b]10/10[/b] - inventive ritual combat mechanics, meaningful roster management, and strong risk/reward systems make Pyre mechanically unique and strategically engaging.

Довольно необычная концепция про местный лимб-чистилище, куда ссылают всех неугодных с одним единственным шансом на амнистию – играть в местные ритуалы, которые прославляют богов. Конечно же, у каждого свое болезненное прошлое и свои мотивы для возвращения в мир реальный. И не обязательно это можно сказать только про спутников нашего главного героя. Напротив, отдельные из них даже не очень и хотят туда – им важнее местная движуха со своими новыми друзьями и соратниками. 

Pyre – довольно редкая игра, где сложно найти для себя причины, чтобы не вернуться в местный мир, перепроходя это чудо на иной манер. Не самое известное детище уже именитой студии, но, для меня – самое, наверное, любимое. Первичное непонимание всего происходящего и того, как визуальную новеллу смешивают с довольно репетативным геймплеем вполне может отпугнуть. Как и сама форма ритуалов, которые или слишком легкие, или ты включаешь местные модификаторы сложности и пытаешься хоть как-то выиграть. Если после Hades решили ознакомиться с другими играми студии – вам сюда. Ну или в Transistor, но это уже совсем другая история.
C'est bien, mécanique de jeu assez originale mais ça devient un peu redondant à la longue. L'histoire n'est pas très développée.
